answers.answer: Build the 10-card deck top to bottom from three separately shuffled tiers: 1 randomly dealt Conflict I card, then 5 randomly dealt Conflict II cards, then all 4 Conflict III cards in shuffled order. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘1 card randomly dealt from the shuffled 4 Conflict I cards; 5 cards randomly dealt from the shuffled 10 Conflict II cards; all 4 Conflict III cards in shuffled order’ and ‘Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader; their third Agent (Swordmaster) is set next to the board and is not yet on their Leader. They have 12 troops total: 3 in their garrison and the other 9 in supply. They start with 1 water and 0 Influence on each of four Faction tracks. Starting VP is 1 in a four-player game and 0 otherwise, so 0 in a three-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘2 Agents on their Leader’ and ‘third Agent (their Swordmaster) next to the game board’; ‘other 12 are your troops,’ with 3 in the garrison; ‘Each player takes 1 water’; four cubes on the bottom spaces; Score marker on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes. You may take your Reveal turn while Agents remain. After it, your turns are skipped for the rest of the Player Turns phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue cards may be played at any point during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns; you cannot play one later in the phase after your Reveal turn because you have no further turns.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘Agent turns are optional: you may take your Reveal turn while you still have Agents left’ and after Reveal ‘your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.’ Plot cards may be played ‘during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.’

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up and use one matching Agent icon to send exactly one Agent to an unoccupied space. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn, and one card cannot send multiple Agents. You must meet the space requirements and pay its costs immediately, before resolving the space or card effects; if you cannot pay, you cannot send the Agent there.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: ‘play one card from your hand face up’; choose ‘only one Agent icon’; ‘one card can't send multiple Agents’; the space must be unoccupied; pay costs and meet requirements before resolving effects.

answers.answer: No. Conspire’s 4-spice entry cost is paid immediately before effects resolve, so the Agent card’s spice gain cannot pay that entry cost when you have only 3 spice. After legally entering and paying the cost, resolve the board-space effect, card’s Agent box, and one-space Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: ‘Costs are paid immediately, before resolving any effects of the space or the played card’; effects of the space, Agent box, and Faction advancement may be gained ‘in any order, after paying the entry cost.’ Actions lists Conspire’s cost as 4 spice.

answers.answer: The maximum is 5 troops: all 3 recruited this turn plus up to 2 more from your garrison. Any recruited troops not deployed remain in your garrison. Rally Troops normally cannot deploy its recruits because it is not a Combat space; its four recruits go to your garrison.
answers.evidence: Deploying: at a Combat space you may deploy ‘any or all troops you recruited this turn ... plus up to two more troops from your garrison.’ ‘Recruited troops you don't deploy go to your garrison.’ Rally Troops is listed as ‘not a Combat space, so they go to your garrison.’

answers.answer: The Reveal turn steps are: (1) reveal all remaining hand cards; (2) resolve the Reveal boxes of those newly revealed cards, in any order; (3) set Combat strength; (4) clean up. Reveal boxes on cards played during Agent turns are not used. During cleanup, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn lists the four steps in order and specifies Reveal boxes apply to ‘cards you just revealed (not of cards played during Agent turns earlier this round)’; cleanup puts all cards from Agent and Reveal turns into the discard pile.

answers.answer: Yes, you may acquire the replacement for a card you just acquired because the Imperium Row refills immediately. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card and split Persuasion from one source across different cards. Unused Persuasion cannot be saved, and acquired cards go to your discard pile and are not used immediately. An Acquire box effect happens once at the moment the card is acquired.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: ‘may pool Persuasion from multiple sources ... and may split Persuasion from a single source’; Persuasion ‘can never be saved’; acquired cards go to discard and ‘You don't use them right away’; Row refills immediately; Acquire box effect applies ‘at the moment you acquire the card.’

answers.answer: With 3 troops in the Conflict and 4 revealed swords, strength is 10 (3 × 2 plus 4 × 1). If your last deployed troop is removed, strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased by any means, including swords. For a value over 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Set Strength: each Conflict troop is 2 and each revealed sword is 1; with no troops strength is 0 and cannot be increased, including by swords. For over 20, flip to the +20 side and start again from the beginning.

answers.answer: Players with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass, starting with the First Player and continuing clockwise. A pass earlier in the phase does not prevent later play. Combat resolves after all players involved pass consecutively. ‘When you win a Conflict’ cards are played only after winning and before moving to the next phase; if such a card is drawn as a victory reward, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: starting with First Player clockwise, each player ‘with at least one troop in the Conflict’ may play or pass; you are not required to pass after a prior pass; resolve after consecutive passes; win-trigger cards are played after winning.

answers.answer: A and B do not win; each receives the second reward for the first-place tie. C and D still compete for third place, so C receives the third reward and D receives none. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, including in two- and three-player games; a tie for third gives nothing. A player with 0 strength gets no reward. After rewards, troops return to each player’s supply, not their garrison.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied for first means no winner and each gets the second reward; in a four-player first-place tie the other two compete for third. A second-place tie gives each the third reward; a third-place tie gives nothing. Zero strength receives no reward; troops go to supply.

answers.answer: In Phase 4: Makers, check The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin; put 1 bonus spice from the bank on each space with no Agent, adding to any accumulated bonus. Normal harvesting happens when an Agent visits: Imperial Basin gives 1 base spice, Hagga Basin 2, and The Great Flat 3, plus any bonus spice on that space. If an Agent moved away and the Maker space is empty during Phase 4, bonus spice accumulates there.
answers.evidence: Makers checks the three named spaces and adds 1 spice to any with no Agent, accumulating bonus spice. The board-space table gives the base harvest plus bonus; the FAQ specifies base amounts; Maker clarification says if an Agent moves away and it is still empty in Phase 4, bonus spice accumulates.

answers.answer: The game ends at the end of the round if any player has 10 or more VP, or if the Conflict Deck is empty (including after the last Conflict has been revealed). Before determining the winner, players may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards. Highest VP wins; ties break in this order: spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Scoring: game end trigger is ‘at the end of a round (Phase 5: Recall)’ with 10+ VP or empty Conflict Deck; first resolve Endgame Intrigue cards; tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, most recent Reveal turn.

answers.answer: The VP for reaching 2 Influence is lost if you drop below 2 and regained if you reach 2 again. The bonus earned at 4 Influence is kept after dropping below 4 and can be earned again by dropping back and re-advancing. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance and its VP; merely tying the holder does not take it, but an opponent who advances to a higher space transfers the token and its VP to them.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: 2 Influence VP is lost below 2 and regained upon returning to 2; the 4 Influence bonus is kept and may be earned again. Alliances: first to 4 takes the token; merely tying does not take it; rising higher transfers it.

answers.answer: If you lose 1 Influence while tied at 5 with two opponents, a previously tied opponent takes the Alliance; because multiple players were tied, you choose which one. If instead you were the only player at 4 and fall to 3, you lose the Alliance; since nobody else is at 4 or higher to take it, return it to the board.
answers.evidence: Alliances: if a holder loses Influence while previously tied, the previously tied player takes it; if several were tied, the holder chooses one. Falling to 3 or less loses the token, and if nobody has 4 or more, return it to the board.

answers.answer: Discarding means taking a card from your hand unless otherwise specified and putting it in your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from your hand, discard pile, or in play to the game box; a Reserve card returns to its Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card instructs you to trash itself. You may not reshuffle an empty deck early just to inspect its top card; reshuffling occurs when you are unable to draw.
answers.evidence: Trashing cards: discard is from hand and goes to discard; trash removes from hand, discard, or in play, while Reserve cards return to Reserve; trashing is optional except for a cost or self-trash instruction. Deck exhaustion says reshuffle when unable to draw and ‘You can't reshuffle early’ to look at the top card.

answers.answer: Control can be won from a Conflict titled for Arrakeen, Carthag, or Imperial Basin; the winner places a Control marker on that space’s flag, replacing an opponent’s marker. Whenever any player (including the controller) sends an Agent to Arrakeen or Carthag, the controller gains 1 Solari; at Imperial Basin, the controller gains 1 spice. When a Conflict card for a space you already control is revealed, you may deploy 1 troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control: winning the named Conflict places a marker, replacing another; controller receives the listed bonus whenever any player visits; when the matching Conflict is revealed, the controller may deploy one troop from supply.

answers.answer: House Hagal is a third Rival in standard two-player games. For setup, choose an unused color, place one cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks and the rest in its supply, with no troops in its garrison; remove the three Arrakeen cards marked 1P, shuffle the remaining House Hagal cards, and place that deck and its three Agents by its supply. It takes one Agent turn after each First Player Agent turn if it has an Agent available; it does not act after the other human’s turns or after a Reveal turn. It has three Agents and never takes a Reveal turn. It collects no resources, earns no VP or Conflict rewards, cannot claim Control, but can take and hold Faction Alliances.
answers.evidence: Two-player House Hagal: setup specifies unused color, starting Influence cubes, no garrison troops, removing 1P cards, shuffled deck and three Agents. It acts after First Player Agent turns, never after other human or Reveal turns, never Reveals, and the overview states its resource, VP, reward, Control, and Alliance limitations.

answers.answer: If a revealed card’s indicated space is occupied, keep revealing until an eligible unoccupied space appears. If the deck is empty or a Reshuffle card appears, reshuffle immediately and continue. Ignore the space’s normal costs, requirements, and effects; resolve only the Hagal card’s icons and instructions. A troop icon recruits from Hagal’s supply, deploying on a Combat space and otherwise placing the troop in its garrison. Whenever Hagal sends an Agent to a Combat space, it must automatically deploy up to 2 additional garrison troops (1 if only one is available, none if empty), even if the card recruited no troops. Harvest Spice follows the card instructions, but harvested bonus spice is removed from the space and returned to the bank. For a two-space card, use only the option matching current conditions; if that option is occupied, draw a new card and do not switch to the other option.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Agent turns specify continued draws for occupied spaces and reshuffling on empty deck or Reshuffle; ignore space costs/requirements/effects; troop recruitment and mandatory Combat deployment; harvested bonus spice goes back to bank; an occupied applicable option on a two-space card means draw again, never switch.

answers.answer: If Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, at the start of Combat reveal a Hagal card; if it is Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Count only its sword icons and add that strength to 2 per deployed troop. Humans may then play Combat Intrigue before resolution. Hagal receives no reward for its rank but occupies that rank when human rewards are assigned. If Hagal wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that Control marker and Hagal does not replace it. A human tie for second receives the third reward even though an ordinary third-place finisher receives no reward in two-player play.
answers.evidence: Combat strength procedure specifies card reveal, reshuffle handling, sword bonus, and 2 strength per deployed troop; humans play Combat Intrigue afterward. Hagal occupies rank but gets no reward; winning on a human-controlled space removes the marker; Combat rules say second-place ties receive the third reward even in two-player games.
